who: Raymond Callahan, military historian at the University of Delaware, PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: Authority for Raymond Callahan cites The East India Company and Army Reform and records University of Delaware in the source note for Churchill (1984).
University article identifies military historian Raymond Callahan, says he received his doctorate from Harvard and joined Delaware's faculty in 1967.
Identifies Callahan as professor emeritus of history, formerly at Delaware for 38 years, with master's and doctoral degrees from Harvard.

notes: The authority's explicit Delaware affiliation, Harvard doctorate and faculty chronology support the match.

who: Clarke A. Chambers, historian of social welfare at the University of Minnesota, PhD Berkeley 1950.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Clarke A. Chambers, associates him with the University of Minnesota, and cites California Farm Organizations.
University oral-history abstract records a history PhD from Berkeley in 1950 and service in Minnesota's History Department from 1951 until retirement in 1990.
Minnesota Libraries identifies Professor Emeritus Clarke Chambers as founder of its Social Welfare History Archives in 1964.

notes: Name, university, doctoral institution and year agree. Retirement in 1990 does not by itself contradict later dissertation completions.

who: Lynda L. Coon, historian of late antiquity and the early Middle Ages at Arkansas, PhD Virginia 1990.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Lynda L. Coon and cites That Gentle Strength (1990).
University article states that Coon earned her history doctorate at Virginia in 1990 and joined Arkansas's History Department that year.
The department lists Lynda Coon as advisor of Natalie Hall's dissertation on the spatial agency of the catacombs.
University faculty recognition page identifies Lynda L. Coon as professor of history and Honors College dean, specializing in the later Roman Empire and early medieval West.

notes: Full name, doctorate and a listed student's advisor agree.

who: Thomas J. Curran, history professor at St. John's University, New York, with a Columbia doctorate.

evidence.says: The 1965–1966 university catalogue lists Thomas J. Curran as assistant professor of history with MA and PhD degrees from Columbia.
The AHA's 1979 meeting program identifies Thomas J. Curran with St. John's University.
The candidate authority identifies Thomas F. Curran, author of Soldiers of Peace.
University library bibliography describes Thomas F. Curran's Soldiers of Peace as partly based on his Notre Dame dissertation of 1993.
Publisher identifies the candidate author as a teacher at Cor Jesu Academy since 2003, previously at Saint Louis University and Notre Dame.

notes: Reject p-4261: the St. John's supervisor is Thomas J. Curran, already holding a Columbia PhD by 1965; the candidate is Thomas F. Curran, whose dissertation was at Notre Dame in 1993.

who: Ronald E. Doel, historian of science at Florida State University, PhD Princeton 1990.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Ronald Edmund Doel, associates him with Princeton, and cites Unpacking a Myth (1990) and Solar System Astronomy in America.
Florida State's faculty profile records a history PhD from Princeton in 1990, arrival at FSU in 2008, and authorship of Solar System Astronomy in America.
FSU's 2008–2009 new faculty directory lists Ronald Doel as associate professor of history with a Princeton PhD and interests in science, environmental history and Cold War studies.

notes: Doctorate, publication and FSU appointment before the listed dissertations agree.

who: Robin F. A. Fabel, historian at Auburn University, PhD Auburn.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Robin F. A. Fabel as author of Bombast and Broadsides.
Publisher identifies Robin F. A. Fabel as associate professor of history at Auburn and lists Bombast and Broadsides among his books.
Auburn's bulletin lists Robin F. A. Fabel as professor emeritus in history, with an Auburn PhD and Oxford MA and BA; the emeritus entry is dated 2001.

notes: Full name, book, institution and doctoral school agree; the sources consulted do not independently establish the doctorate's year.

WVU's faculty profile identifies Elizabeth Fones-Wolf as professor emeritus of history, records her Massachusetts PhD in 1990, and identifies Selling Free Enterprise as her first book.

who: Robert F. Himmelberg, historian of US political and economic history at Fordham, PhD Penn State 1963.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Robert F. Himmelberg as author of The Origins of the National Recovery Administration.
His institutional CV records a history PhD at Penn State in 1963, Fordham appointments from 1961 onward, and The Origins of the National Recovery Administration among his books.
Fordham lists Robert Himmelberg as mentor of Philip R. Silvia's 1973 dissertation, The Spindle City, matching the supplied student and title.

notes: Exact doctorate and faculty chronology agree, with direct corroboration of a listed student's supervision.
